sentences.text: The petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Gaurav Kejriwal and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Kuldeep Bhati and PSI Manisha Bansal from Police Station Madhu Vihar, Delhi.
6. The present dispute is an offshoot of criminal discord between the complainant and the petitioner No. 1.
Allegations under Section 354 are levelled against the petitioner.
The matter has been amicably settled between the parties including the matrimonial cases.
Affidavit in this regard is on record.

7. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner No. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 12.11.2016 according to Hindu Rites and customs and no child was born out of the said wedlock.
It is stated that due to temperamental differences, both the parties have started living separately from February, 2022.

On the complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing No.
563/2022 registered at Police Station Madhu Vihar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 323/354/354(B)/506/509 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) against petitioners.

During the pendency of the present FIR, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes before the Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 12.06.2023 entered into between them.

It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Settlement Deed dated 12.06.2023 entered into between them.

9. It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.

10. The petitioner had paid a sum of Rs. 3,50,000/- in three installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 1,50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 in the first motion petition.
b. Second installment of Rs. 1,50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of second motion petition.
c. Third/Final instalment of Rs. 50,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

12. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.
